value.rationale: Permanent active-affine-manifold identification is a natural and materially different property from asymptotic convergence in a randomized constrained optimizer: skipped proximal calls can repeatedly destroy feasibility, unlike standard deterministic proximal gradient. The result gives the complete iff parameter classification, explicit inter-prox renewal distribution, and unique optimal expected latency across all resonances. This reveals an arithmetic tuning discontinuity even within the source method's convergence-safe range. Its limited isotropic-quadratic applicability and finite-precision sensitivity are explicitly acknowledged.
